summary.text:
A cheap book with a visible cliff. Redbridge holds £564.171m at an average 3.53%, against a CFR of £749.253m — the reconciliation ties to the penny once the £111.311m of other long-term liabilities is taken out, leaving £73.771m under-borrowed. The General Fund PWLB averages 2.89% and the 2019 fifty-year inflation-linked bond costs 2.03%.

£108.5m, 19.2% of the book, matures inside two years: £55.000m under 12 months and £53.500m in the year after. Replacing that on today's curve is a different proposition from the rate it currently carries. The year's own borrowing shows the gap — £85m of new General Fund PWLB and £35m for the HRA at an average 4.25%.

Two things stand out for accuracy. Their statement that the HRA certainty rate is 0.6% below standard is exactly right and matches every other council we have read. And no PWLB was rescheduled because the differential gave no benefit — a conclusion that changes as the curve moves, which is why it is worth being able to check daily rather than annually.

officer.subject: £108.5m of your borrowing reprices before 2028
officer.body:
Hi Bola,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts ahead of the outturn going to Council on 24 September. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Your report is a properly complete set: PI 3 reconciles to the penny once the £111.311m of other long-term liabilities comes out, which is more than we can say for most.

A cross-check first. We hold all 53 of your PWLB loans at 31 March, £479.17m, which is your table exactly. Our weighted rate runs a little above your 2.89% and 4.19% splits, which we'd put down to effective-interest accounting on your side rather than a difference in the loans themselves — worth a look if it matters to you.

The number that stands out is the near maturity. £108.5m falls due inside two years — £55.000m under twelve months and £53.500m in the year after — against a book averaging 3.53%. The General Fund PWLB costs 2.89% and the 2019 bond 2.03%, so this is genuinely cheap debt reaching the end of its run rather than expensive debt you'd want to move. Five-year certainty money is 5.34% today and ten-year 5.83%, and against a late-February strategy date the whole curve is roughly 0.6% higher.

Your own borrowing already shows the gap. £85m of new General Fund PWLB and £35m for the HRA at an average 4.25%, with the HRA certainty rate 0.6% below standard — which, incidentally, is stated correctly at 5.7 and often isn't elsewhere.

The other line worth revisiting periodically is 6.16, where no PWLB was rescheduled because the differential gave no cost benefit. That's a conclusion that changes as the curve moves, and it's the reason we price every loan daily against the DMO repayment curve rather than annually. Yours is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. The monthly sector picture is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — July was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%, which tells you how much appetite there is before you roll rather than after. Rates at both fixings are at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard.

On training, three fit Redbridge: Strategic PWLB borrowing, for the £108.5m; HRA borrowing and the certainty rate, given the £219.621m HRA book; and our liability benchmark pathway, which is interactive and built on live data — you already report PI 9, and it's worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes. For members, Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) is written for exactly the scrutiny this report gets. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Outturn 2025/26, Cabinet, 16 July 2026 (Overview & Scrutiny, 13 July 2026).
